newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss diplomat urges help for North Korea.
newsitem.headline: Swiss diplomat urges help for North Korea.

text.p: A senior Swiss diplomat said on Monday that North Korea faces a catastrophic famine unless the international community comes to its aid.

"The situation in North Korea is even worse than I had imagined," said Walter Fust, director of the Swiss government's Office for Development and Cooperation at a news briefing after a visit to the communist country.
"It is now to be hoped that the international community of nations will no longer tie aid to politics. Otherwise they will share the blame for a catastrophe of hunger," Fust said.
North Korea's food supply, damaged by flooding in the past two years, was again critically reduced by a recent drought.
Fust said North Korea was lacking 500,000 tonnes of the 800,000 tonnes of grain it needed.
He said an estimated 40 percent of North Korean children are undernourished. He added that mainly children and the elderly were affected by cuts in food rations.
At the same time, he said that industry was pinched by lack of electricity and oil.

Since autumn 1994, Switzerland has provided 10 million Swiss francs of direct aid to North Korea, plus another six million in goods. A new aid shipment should arrive there in two weeks. Switzerland also will step up its aid, especially in cooperation with international charitable organisations, he said.
